tapeLine: Wednesday 25 November: S&P 500 −0.25% to 7,182.78; Nasdaq Composite −0.62% to 23,585.80; Dow +0.33% (+164.25) to 50,182.95, after erasing a drop of about 1,100 points (CNBC; Investing.com; Yahoo Finance, 25 Nov). US markets are closed today for Thanksgiving.
matters:
Wednesday was a round trip. The Nasdaq Composite fell roughly 4% in the morning (CNN had 3.8% at the low, Yahoo Finance 4.1% by about 11 a.m.) and the Dow was down about 1,100 points, before both recovered most of it into the close; the Dow finished up for a third straight session (CNN; Yahoo Finance; CNBC, 25 Nov). Nvidia fell as much as 9.1% intraday and closed −3.91%, with wraps tying the selling to doubts about AI spending and returns, new tariff proposals and rate-hike worries. The same day S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia’s AA ratings on CreditWatch negative, citing governance and key-person risk after Jensen Huang’s reinstatement on 23 Nov; S&P said any cut would likely be one notch, and Moody’s left its rating unchanged (BigGo Finance; CNBC; Benzinga; AOL, 25 Nov).

The 8:30 data ran hot on growth and core inflation. Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualized from 3.4% (BEA). October PCE prices rose 0.3% m/m and 3.8% y/y; core rose 0.3% m/m and 3.3% y/y, up from 3.1% (BEA). Initial claims fell to 189,000 (gsmglobalnews; theintelligent.us). Treasuries rallied anyway: CNBC had the 10-year at 4.866%, more than 3 bp lower, and prediction-market and futures-based estimates put a 25 bp December hike at roughly 92–98% (CNBC; predictionmarketspicks, 25 Nov). USTR also published proposed Section 301 overcapacity tariffs on 14 of the 16 economies it investigated; nothing takes effect before a comment period running to 5 Jan 2027 (Holland & Knight; Kelley Drye; KPMG, 25 Nov).

overnight: Latest confirmed close — Wednesday 25 November: S&P 500 7,182.78 (−0.25%); Nasdaq Composite 23,585.80 (−0.62%); Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%) (CNBC; Investing.com; Yahoo Finance, 25 Nov).

Nvidia — fell as much as 9.1% intraday and closed −3.91% (BigGo Finance, 25 Nov). S&P Global Ratings placed its AA issuer and senior unsecured ratings on CreditWatch negative over board-oversight and succession concerns; a verdict is due within up to 90 days. Huang is scheduled before House committees on 1 Dec (Benzinga; AOL; Seoul Economic Daily, 25–26 Nov).
Dell — after Tuesday’s results the shares were −7.25% at $273.87 intraday Wednesday per Benzinga; the Wednesday close was not confirmed and is left out (Benzinga, 25 Nov).
deals: Lukoil International / Boehly-led consortium — a consortium led by Todd Boehly signed an agreement for Lukoil International GmbH, which holds Lukoil’s overseas operations; reported as a securities swap of about $10 billion, with one report valuing the assets at about $16 billion. Requires OFAC approval (Ecofin Agency; UNN, 26 Nov).
macro: Q3 GDP, second estimate — 4.3% annualized, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the 3.4% advance estimate, mainly on investment and consumer spending (BEA, 25 Nov).
October personal income and outlays — PCE price index +0.3% m/m, +3.8% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.3% y/y (from 3.1%). Personal income +0.7%; spending +0.3%. Next release 23 Dec (BEA, 25 Nov).
Jobless claims, week to 21 Nov — initial claims 189,000; four-week average 196,000; continuing claims 1.697 million (gsmglobalnews; theintelligent.us, 25 Nov).
Durable goods, October — orders +0.2%; core capital goods orders +1.2% (theintelligent.us; edgeconsultancykw; cbnc, 25 Nov).

Section 301 — USTR made affirmative overcapacity determinations for 14 of 16 economies and proposed tariffs, up to 35% for Vietnam and up to 25% for several others including India, Korea, Taiwan and Malaysia; no determinations yet for Mexico or Norway. Goods under Section 232 tariffs are excluded. Comments due 5 Jan 2027, hearings in January (Holland & Knight; Kelley Drye; KPMG, 25 Nov).
Fed — December hike priced at roughly 92–98% depending on the measure; decision 9 Dec (predictionmarketspicks; Seoul Economic Daily, 25–26 Nov).
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: A sharp morning tech flush, then a recovery to a mixed close, on hot core PCE, a 4.3% GDP revision and new tariff proposals, into a holiday.
regime.sizing: Friday is a shortened 1:00 p.m. session after a closed Thursday; liquidity is thin by schedule.

secondOrder: Bonds rallied on a day core inflation and growth both came in above consensus. The Dow has now risen three straight sessions while the Nasdaq fell in two of them. A ratings agency flagged governance risk at Nvidia on the same day its shares swung more than 5 points intraday. Observations, not forecasts.

The prior brief carried a core PCE consensus of 3.2% y/y. It printed 3.3% (BEA, 25 Nov).
The prior brief carried a Q3 GDP second-estimate consensus of 3.4–3.6%. It printed 4.3%, well above (BEA, 25 Nov).
The prior brief carried a jobless-claims consensus of about 200K. Claims printed 189,000 (gsmglobalnews, 25 Nov).
The prior brief carried a durable goods consensus of +1.1% (Longbridge; Buglecall +2.5%). Orders rose 0.2% (theintelligent.us, 25 Nov).

The prior brief reported (on unnamed sources, unconfirmed) that USTR might announce Section 301 overcapacity results this week. USTR published proposed tariffs on 25 Nov (Holland & Knight; KPMG, 25 Nov).

The prior brief reported futures lower Wednesday morning. The S&P and Nasdaq did close lower, but far above their lows, and the Dow closed higher; a direction call on futures is not a close call, so this is left ungraded.
The prior brief listed the Fed Beige Book at 14:00 ET; its contents were not confirmed in this morning’s search and are left out.
